principle: Production agents require system design, tool contracts, retrieval, reliability, security, evals, observability, product trust, and procedural skills before implementation.

disciplines.name: System Design
disciplines.purpose: Define components, ownership, data flow, orchestration, model routing, state, jobs, approvals, and failure boundaries.
p0_blockers: multi-tool agent with no system diagram
no owner for state or memory
no routing policy for multiple models or providers

disciplines.name: Tool and Contract Design
disciplines.purpose: Make every tool callable through strict schemas, examples, output contracts, validation, permissions, and failure behavior.
p0_blockers: write tools with no approval policy
vague tool inputs
no output contract for downstream steps

disciplines.name: Retrieval Engineering
disciplines.purpose: Design source inventory, chunking, embeddings, metadata, reranking, citations, freshness, and retrieval evals.
p0_blockers: RAG assumed without corpus design
no relevance metric
no stale-data handling for fresh-answer use cases

disciplines.name: Reliability Engineering
disciplines.purpose: Control failure through timeouts, retries, backoff, circuit breakers, job state, idempotency, fallbacks, and rollback.
p0_blockers: unbounded retries
no timeout policy
no rollback path for external writes

disciplines.name: Security and Safety
disciplines.purpose: Bound prompt injection, input validation, output filtering, least privilege, tenant isolation, secret handling, and external action controls.
p0_blockers: public/send/delete/spend action without approval
tool output trusted blindly
no tenant boundary for memory or retrieval

disciplines.name: Evaluation and Observability
disciplines.purpose: Make behavior measurable through traces, tool-call logs, retrieved-context logs, evals, golden examples, metrics, and drift detection.
p0_blockers: no way to reproduce bad answers
no eval set for core workflows
no trace of tool inputs or retrieval context

disciplines.name: Product Trust and UX
disciplines.purpose: Design confidence, uncertainty, memory visibility, evidence trails, approval surfaces, escalation, graceful errors, and rollback affordances.
p0_blockers: user cannot inspect why the agent answered or acted
memory changes are hidden
no escalation path for low confidence

skill_trust_levels.name: Spec Only
skill_trust_levels.description: Skill candidate only; no installed instructions or executable code.

skill_trust_levels.name: Instructions Only
skill_trust_levels.description: SKILL.md instructions with no executable scripts.

skill_trust_levels.name: Read-Only Scripted
skill_trust_levels.description: Scripts may read local files or validate artifacts, but must not mutate external systems.

skill_trust_levels.name: Controlled External Tooling
skill_trust_levels.description: Skill may call APIs, CLIs, MCP tools, browser flows, or Computer Use inside strict boundaries.

skill_trust_levels.name: Public, Paid, Destructive, or Autonomous
skill_trust_levels.description: Skill can publish, send, delete, spend, mutate production data, or run unattended.

skill_archetypes.name: Capture Signal
skill_archetypes.purpose: Turn raw user, file, browser, or platform inputs into classified domain signals.

skill_archetypes.name: Update Memory
skill_archetypes.purpose: Propose and apply durable memory changes with approval and audit history.

skill_archetypes.name: Retrieve Context
skill_archetypes.purpose: Fetch, rank, cite, and package relevant knowledge for downstream reasoning.

skill_archetypes.name: Generate Artifact
skill_archetypes.purpose: Create a user-visible artifact from a brief, retrieved context, and memory.

skill_archetypes.name: Critique and Score
skill_archetypes.purpose: Evaluate an output against rubrics, evidence, safety, policy, and product-specific quality bars.

skill_archetypes.name: Prepare External Action
skill_archetypes.purpose: Prepare public, paid, destructive, or externally visible actions for explicit approval.

skill_archetypes.name: Run Routine
skill_archetypes.purpose: Run recurring or event-triggered work with bounded inputs, outputs, approvals, and failure handling.

skill_archetypes.name: Research Latest Information
skill_archetypes.purpose: Route fresh-information tasks to web-grounded research providers, browser research, or approved search tools with citations.

skill_archetypes.name: Orchestrate Model Route
skill_archetypes.purpose: Choose the right model, provider, or tool surface for a task based on freshness, coding, reasoning, cost, latency, and governance needs.
